t: The only kingdom within the Holy Roman Empire, ruled from Prague, whose king was one of the electors of the King of the Romans.
Under Charles IV Prague became an imperial capital with Central Europe’s first university, founded in 1348.
Its Hussite reformation predated Luther by a century, and the Defenestration of Prague in 1618 began the Thirty Years War.
dyk: The Teutonic Knights’ fortress of Königsberg, founded in 1255, is traditionally said to have been named in honour of King Ottokar II of Bohemia, who had joined their crusade.
ev: The Golden Bull of Sicily makes the Bohemian royal title hereditary
Ottokar II is defeated and killed at the Battle on the Marchfeld
Charles IV founds the university of Prague and the New Town
Jan Hus is burned at the Council of Constance, sparking the Hussite revolution
Moderate forces defeat the radical Hussites at the Battle of Lipany
The estates elect Ferdinand I, beginning Habsburg rule
The Protestant estates are crushed at the Battle of White Mountain
Czechoslovakia is proclaimed in Prague, with Bohemia at its core
